theorem.formal_statement: Holding a row's registered instruction set and checker parameters fixed, any two nonempty responses with the same checker pass vector receive the same frozen LiveBench IF row score regardless of base-task semantic quality.
theorem.corollary_1: A response that passes every registered legacy checker for a row receives row score 1 even if no semantic-seed generator was used.
theorem.corollary_2: Semantic-seed generation is therefore not a logical prerequisite for LIVEBENCH_IF_GE_65_7; it is optional unless needed instrumentally to satisfy a registered checker.
theorem.corollary_3: The score-closure route can reduce to prompt-only legacy constraint recognition, deterministic witness construction, exact legacy checker postvalidation, and sound aggregate score-mass lower bounds.
